main_body: Sci-fi tower building: a hipped, sloped roof over a windowed band, a narrow shaft, a wide lower sloped roof, and a door front below
top_band: At x=24 the upper roof slope runs rows 10-16: light blue-grey L148 (rows 10-14) then lighter L178 (rows 15-16), under the antenna. Below it is a dark edge row at 17-18, then the window band. The lower roof slope at rows 52-62 follows the same pattern.
evidence: Both roofs are drawn as trapezoid slopes that narrow towards the back, so they read as surfaces seen from above. The upper roof is 7+ rows tall, with a lighter front-edge line at rows 15-16 and a dark eave row at 17-18 above the windows. The windows have dark inset frames. The lower roof is about 10 rows tall, with panel seams and a lighter lip at row 61, above the door front at rows 64-79. The door has an inset recess and dark frame. No receding isometric side faces. Every major part satisfies the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185 in the references. Its flat-fill coverage is 21% against 0% for both references, visible in the large uniform dark front and wall areas and the flat shaft. 84% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% in the references. The outlines are therefore near-black sticker lines instead of dark tones of the adjacent material. The roof slopes show only about 3-4 blue-grey steps with panel seams and no per-element grain or texture dots. The median of 10 colours per tile is comparable to the stone reference, but that tile figure is not enough to offset the neutral outline, the flat fills and the thin palette.
